en.title: Why Benedict Cumberbatch Is Suddenly Everywhere in Magic: The Gathering
en.summary: A surprising number of characters portrayed by Benedict Cumberbatch are appearing in upcoming Magic: The Gathering sets. This unique crossover is raising eyebrows among fans and sparking discussions about the game's creative direction.
en.body:
Magic: The Gathering's latest spoiler season for the upcoming **Star Trek** set has revealed a rather peculiar detail: a reskinned version of the powerful **Sheoldred, the Apocalypse** card now features art depicting Khan from the 2013 film *Star Trek Into Darkness*. What makes this particularly noteworthy is that the likeness used is unmistakably that of actor **Benedict Cumberbatch**, who portrayed Khan in the film. Wizards of the Coast securing actor likenesses for these crossover cards is a significant development, but it has led to an interesting observation: the actor's face, or at least characters he's famously played, is appearing on multiple **Magic: The Gathering** cards this year.

This isn't an isolated incident tied solely to the **Star Trek** universe. Fans have also pointed out that the recently released **Marvel Super Heroes** set includes a **Doctor Strange** card whose art is heavily influenced by **Benedict Cumberbatch's** portrayal of the Sorcerer Supreme in the Marvel Cinematic Universe. The convergence of these two major franchises, featuring the same prominent actor's likeness, has sparked considerable discussion within the **Magic: The Gathering** community. It’s a curious choice that goes beyond simply licensing intellectual property; it’s about bringing specific, recognizable on-screen personas into the game.

## A Familiar Face Across Universes

The trend is set to continue with the next major **Magic: The Gathering** crossover, which will delve into the world of **The Hobbit**. While a return to Middle-earth is always a welcome prospect for many players, it appears this set will also feature characters brought to life by **Benedict Cumberbatch**. This means that a single actor's distinctive features will grace cards across at least three distinct, major franchise crossovers within a relatively short period. This strategy, while potentially appealing to fans of both **Magic** and these iconic film properties, raises questions about the long-term aesthetic direction of the game's Universes Beyond line. Is this a deliberate effort to leverage popular actors, or a surprising coincidence that has manifested into a unique collectible phenomenon?

## Community Reactions and Future Implications

The prevalence of **Benedict Cumberbatch** across these diverse **Magic: The Gathering** sets has certainly generated buzz online. Many fans are amused by the sheer coincidence, while others are keen to see how these character interpretations will translate into gameplay mechanics. The decision to use specific actor likenesses, especially for iconic roles, adds a layer of authenticity but also invites comparisons and critiques, as seen with the **Sheoldred** reskin. For dedicated players and collectors, these cards represent not just powerful game pieces but also tangible connections to beloved cinematic moments and the actors who brought them to life. The ongoing presence of **Cumberbatch's** characters suggests a deliberate approach by Wizards of the Coast to lean into recognizable celebrity portrayals for future crossovers.

## What's Next

With **Star Trek** spoilers well underway and **The Hobbit** set on the horizon, players can anticipate more details about these **Benedict Cumberbatch**-associated cards in the coming weeks. The **Star Trek** set is expected to launch soon, with **The Hobbit** set to follow. Further announcements regarding specific card reveals and release dates for both are anticipated.

content_raw: With MagicCon Amsterdam right around the corner, Wizards of the Coast has begun spoiler season for their next crossover set in Magic: The Gathering: Star Trek. While the legendary science-fiction franchise may seem like an odd fit for a trading card game that’s ultimately about wizards flinging spells at each other, space (aka the final frontier) is no stranger to the game. Just last year Magic went to space with the excellent Edge of Eternities set, and the gameplay design was so good it ended up being my favorite set of the year. What’s odd about Star Trek spoiler season though is a particular card that’s being printed on its bonus sheet. As revealed earlier today, the set features a reprint of Sheoldred, The Apocalypse reskinned as Kahn from the 2013 film Star Trek Into Darkness. One of the main selling points of Magic’s Star Trek set is that Wizards of the Coast has obtained the rights to use the likeness of every actor they depict on the card, which means that Sheoldred--instead of being a female phyrexian nightmare being--is now just… Benedict Cumberbatch? Outside of being a bit bummed that a reprint for a $80+ card is being sullied with art from a J.J. Abrams film, it got me thinking. There’s a lot of Benedict Cumberbatch in Magic: The Gathering this year for some reason. Not the actor himself, per se, but characters he’s depicted on screen. For example, the Marvel Super Heroes set just released a Doctor Strange card that has art very clearly influenced by his on screen depiction played by Cumberbatch. Weird that it happened not once but twice, but what if I told you it’s actually happening three times? Following Star Trek, the next MTG crossover set is based on The Hobbit, and while a return to Middle-Earth is always welcome, it allows yet another character that Cumberbatch has portrayed to be depicted in Magic: The Gathering. The card this time is Smaug the Magnificent, and it actually features a chase printing that is the headliner card of the entire Hobbit set. Theoretically, this means that if you build a Mardu (red, white, and black for non-players) deck, you can have every Benedict Cumberbatch card be playable in your gameplan if you so desire. What other universes can Magic: The Gathering depict to add even more Benedict Cumberbatch? Is this secretly their way of testing the water for casting him in the announced Magic: The Gathering streaming adaptation? Who knows really. I just know that I’m tired.
